title: Fibrewise dense relative rational charts and strict birational laws
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X,Y$ be schemes over $S$. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic fibre products [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset X$ is fibrewise dense over $S$ if for every $s\in S$, the inverse image of $U$ in $X_s$ is dense. A relative rational chart from $X$ to $Y$ consists of an $S$-scheme $D$ and $S$-morphisms $i:D\to X$, $h:D\to Y$; it is a rational representative when $i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and its image is fibrewise dense over $S$. Two representatives agree if on an $S$-dense open of $X$ contained in both domains their maps coincide. An $S$-rational map is an equivalence class of these representatives; a representative is $S$-birational if $h$ is also an open immersion with $S$-dense image. For a chart $m:D\to Y$ with inclusion $i:D\hookrightarrow Y\times_SY$, the universal translations are $\Phi=(\operatorname{pr}_1i,m)$ and $\Psi=(m,\operatorname{pr}_2i)$. Associativity as an $S$-rational map means that on an $S$-dense open $A\subset(Y\times_SY)\times_SY$, both pairs $(x,y),(y,z)$ and both outer pairs $(xy,z),(x,yz)$ lift to $D$, and the resulting morphisms $A\to Y$ are equal. The chart is strict if it is rational and associative, the translations are open immersions, and the images of $i,\Phi,\Psi$ are dense in every fibre of each of the two projections $Y\times_SY\to Y$. Thus $D\simeq V=\Phi(D)$ and $D\simeq W=\Psi(D)$ are the strictness charts. This predicate is used on smooth separated finite-type $S$-schemes with nonempty fibres. Base change of raw charts along $g:T\to S$ is the actual pullback of $D,i,h$ via $\mathrm{Over.pullback}(g)$. For a law its inclusion is followed by the canonical product comparison $(Y\times_SY)_T\simeq Y_T\times_TY_T$; its domain remains $D_T$ and its multiplication morphism is $m_T$.
